answer: Let each proposer bond b_i and commit z_i to a liquidity sink; a Sybil swarm of n agents pays capital C(n)=Σb_i+λn(n-1)/2, where λ encodes quadratic slashing erosion triggered by invalid votes. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay bounds plume expansion per slot, so marginal cost dC/dn=b+λn rises faster than extractable value V(n)=γn/(1+κn). Because V(n)-C(n)<0 for n≥1, expected utility is negative; pigment of state is minted only behind a mesa of bonded quorum, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium where no deviating cluster profits.
